newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR MONACO-PSG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR MONACO-PSG.

text.p: Facts and figures for Sunday's French first division match between Monaco and Paris St Germain at the Louis II stadium.
Monaco: Founded in 1924 as Association Sportive de Monaco, joined French league as a professional team in 1948. They have won the French first division championship five times.
Major honours: League champions: 1961, 1963, 1978, 1982, 1988. French Cup winners: 1960, 1963, 1980, 1985, 1991.
Ground: Stade Louis II, capacity 18,500 (15,000 seated). Record number of spectators: 22,000 v AS Roma of Italy in March 1992.
Trainer: Jean Tigana.
Record league appearances: Jean-Luc Ettori 602.
Record number of goals: Delio Onnis 157.
Paris St Germain: Founded in 1970. They have won the French league title twice.
Major honours: League champions: 1986, 1994. French Cup winners: 1982, 1983, 1993, 1995. French League Cup winners: 1995. European Cup Winners' Cup champions: 1996.
Ground: Parc des Princes, capacity 48,712. Record number of spectators: 49,575 v Waterschei of Belgium in March 1983.
Trainer: Ricardo (Ricardo Gomes Raymundo)
Record league appearances: Jean-Marc Pilgoret 370.
Record number of goals: Mustapha Dahleb 84.
Monaco v Paris St Germain league meetings at Stade Louis II in last five years: 1-0, 3-1, 1-1, 2-1, 1-0.
Fascinating facts:
- Monaco president Jean-Louis Campora, a 55-year-old doctor who also presides over the principality's parliament, has been in charge of the club for 22 years.
- They belong to a second wave of French clubs founded between the two world wars (the first wave came at the turn of the century).

- Monaco made a qualitative leap under current Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger in the late 1980s and early 1990s when they became regular qualifiers for European competition and reached the 1992 Cup Winners' Cup final.

- They almost always play against bigger crowds away than at home where their average last season was just over 6,000, a third of the capacity at the Stade Louis II. But football followers in the principality claim it is not indifference and that such an average is good when they are drawing on a population of only 30,000 and environs boosting the figure to no more than 100,000.
- Monaco have an annual budget of 110 million francs ($22 million), about half of which comes from a state subsidy.

- Paris St Germain are a young club founded on 12 August 1970 by merging the interests of leading Parisian personalities for a big club in the capital with the St-Germain-en-Laye team that had just been promoted to the second division. In one season, the new PSG won promotion and so celebrated their first anniversary in the top flight.

- In the 1971/72 season there was a split in the Parisian and St Germain branches of the liaison. Paris FC stayed in the first division and PSG regained their amateur roots in the third division. Within two years PSG returned to the first division and have never again looked back. Ironically, Paris FC were relegated just as PSG were promoted.
- Only Nantes (since 1963) and Metz (since 1967) have been in the first division longer without interruption than PSG.
- PSG played three French Cup finals in four years, winning the trophy in 1982 and 1983 and losing the 1985 final to Monaco.

- PSG went a club record 26 matches unbeaten on their way to their first league title in 1986 and broke the record with 27 games without defeat when they took their second title in the 1993/4 season under Portuguese coach Artur Jorge and with their present trainer Ricardo in central defence.
- In 1991, the financially strapped PSG were bought by the private cable television network Canal Plus.
